parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a clean-room reverse engineering of the age CLI from bundled docs and observed executable behavior, including CLI flags, identity/recipient formats, passphrase behavior, armor, and wire compatibility.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent split early work into docs_probe and cli_probe, later relied mostly on parent implementation and a late mac_probe child for MAC search; ownership of final clean packaging stayed with the parent.
parallel.implementation: Built a Go implementation with age format, recipient, key parsing, scrypt, stream, and utility packages, but remained stuck on header MAC and payload compatibility late in the run.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted tree contained implementation files plus debug/probe test artifacts such as debug_test.go, mac_probe_test.go, and tmp_probe paths, and the official artifact did not validate cleanly.
parallel.verification: Local builds succeeded at points and the agent ran oracle interop probes, but those probes exposed no-identity and bad-header-MAC failures and the late mac_probe reported no matches.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with returncode 143, process_ok false, unresolved MAC work, debug/probe artifacts present, and official compile_failed with 839 tests not run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room age CLI requirements and mapped docs, help/version behavior, error messages, recipient and identity files, passphrase prompts, armor, and SSH support.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One root agent owned investigation, implementation, build, artifact replacement, and final reporting without subagent handoffs or child lifecycle management.
serial.implementation: Implemented a standalone Go rewrite with CLI parsing, key and SSH parsing, passphrase handling, scrypt, and format code, then added a compile script and built ./executable.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Renamed the oracle aside during development, built the replacement executable through compile.sh, and ended with an artifact package that status marked artifact_ok true.
serial.verification: Ran local compile, version, unknown-flag, passphrase, and self-roundtrip checks; cross-checks against the oracle showed remaining header/payload cryptographic framing mismatch.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final response explicitly says benchmark-complete wire compatibility was not closed, so the official solution_passed remained false despite process_ok and artifact_ok.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room requirement and the need to match the provided age executable using docs and CLI probing only.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and recognized the same clean-room executable and documentation constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No meaningful requirement difference; both attempted the same age CLI, but serial preserved a clearer final limitation while parallel never reached clean closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split initial docs and CLI probing into child agents while the parent retained implementation and final artifact work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing, implementation, packaging, and reporting in one continuous owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child lifecycle boundaries for investigation; serial had no child ownership boundary to manage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received at least one nested CLI/docs report through agent listing, but active top-level probes were still running when interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial converted its own probing into an implementation plan without inter-agent transfer or handoff compression.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had handoff and lifecycle risk around child results; serial's context stayed inside one root thread.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a Go implementation and added debug tests while continuing to chase cryptographic mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a Go implementation, fixed build dependencies, and installed a replacement executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both paths reached substantial code, but parallel kept debug/probe code in the project while serial emphasized final deliverable hygiene.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel explicitly interrupted docs_probe and cli_probe while they were still running, and those child trajectories record aborted turns.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no spawned children and no child result lifecycle to join or interrupt.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material lifecycle difference is parallel's early child termination versus serial's uninterrupted single-thread result path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final status lists debug/probe test files and tmp_probe artifacts in the workspace submitted for evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial added compile.sh, replaced the root executable, and status recorded artifact packing success.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's final tree was contaminated by unfinished probe artifacts and failed artifact validation; serial delivered a cleaner buildable artifact despite behavioral gaps.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran interop checks that still failed and a late MAC probe reported no matches before the official compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran compile and self-roundtrip smoke tests, but acknowledged that oracle wire compatibility remained unresolved.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification remained exploratory and left failing probe tests; serial verification was cleaner but insufficient for full evaluator compatibility.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed multi-agent budget, timed out, and ended with process_ok false before clean packaging.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished with returncode 0, process_ok true, and a final response that scoped the remaining limitation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was timeout-driven and compile-failed; serial closure was explicit and buildable but incomplete.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official status records make this a both_fail pair, not a discordant pass/fail outcome. The important task-solving difference is failure mode: parallel timed out and its artifact failed compilation with debug/probe files present, while serial completed normally with a packaged executable but remained behaviorally incomplete on exact age wire-format compatibility.
parallel_contributors: Explicit interruption of active docs_probe and cli_probe removed normal finalized child handoffs from the early investigation path.
Late work remained focused on unresolved header MAC and payload framing, with debug and probe tests left in the evaluated tree.
The process ended with returncode 143, artifact_ok false, process_ok false, and official compile_failed.
serial_contributors: Single-agent ownership avoided child lifecycle loss and ended with artifact_ok true and process_ok true.
The serial final response acknowledged local smoke success but incomplete oracle wire compatibility.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations struggled with cryptographic wire compatibility, especially header MAC and payload framing.
Serial's failure is best explained as incomplete behavioral fidelity rather than a parallel coordination error.
evaluator_effects: Parallel failed at compile_failed before tests ran, while serial had no compile error code but still did not pass; both show 839 tests not run in current official summaries.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative explanation with no official outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized adverse parallel process event, not an exclusive root cause

There were no separately completed component implementations needing an unowned integration owner; child work was investigative.
The parent handled build and final workspace activity; compile failure came from unfinished/probe artifacts, not an unassigned assembly step.
The parent owned the end-to-end path from implementation through tests and delivery; lifecycle interruption is the direct issue.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; docs and CLI probes overlapped with parent workspace work.
The parallel attempt did not merely complete all investigation as a first phase before implementation; the direct failure was interrupted children.
MAC work was unfinished, but the evidence does not show auxiliary workers displaced a clearly underallocated critical path beyond the same interruption/deadline chain.
The run used many subagent/tool calls and timed out, but no separate excessive fan-out episode is proven apart from the retained child-interruption chain.
The interrupted children were scoped as probes, not a demonstrably oversized child implementation assignment that failed to checkpoint.
Child briefs are redacted and the visible evidence does not prove a parent-known requirement was omitted and then followed incorrectly by a child.
No separately owned child components were delivered with incompatible interfaces; the parent implementation carried the source integration burden.
There is no proof that a known finding disappeared during transfer and caused repeated or incorrect work.
A long nested report was visible, but the record does not prove it was too large to consume or that size caused the unfinished action.
No receiver action is shown to depend on a superseded handoff state, so the stale-handoff boundary is absent.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.

The visible retries and late probes used current workspace state; no replacement agent repeated prior work because it lacked inherited checkpoints.

The workspace was shared, but the observed problem is leftover probe artifacts and interrupted work, not unstable provenance from unspecific concurrent writes.
